sources.citation: Gatschet, Albert S. 1891. The Karankawa Indians, the coast people of Texas. Archaeological and Ethnological Papers of the Peabody Museum 1(2). Cambridge, Mass.
sources.note: Aranama words are not reprinted here; p. 79 only reports Old Simon's mention of the 'Kharimame, Khaimi,me or Hanama' (= Xaranames) and p. 108 'Accentuation' paragraph is about Karankawa, not Aranama.
No descriptive references listed (only the Swanton 1940 and Zamponi 2023 overviews in the target record).
Reports the corpus as himiyána 'water', himiaʹna tsaʹyi 'give me water!'; no stress statement. Used only to identify Zamponi 2023 and Mithun 2017 as the modern secondary discussions.

sources.citation: Swanton, John R. 1940. Linguistic material from the tribes of Southern Texas and Northeastern Mexico. Bureau of American Ethnology Bulletin 127. Washington: GPO.
sources.note: Nothing about Aranama stress. The whole Aranama entry is 'WORDS IN ARANAMA: himia'na tsa'yi, give me water! / himiya'na, water.' (p. 124, PDF p. 132). Phonetics pp. 9-10 say only 'The two Aranama words yield the following phonetics' [sound list] and, of accent marks, 'The accents in Comecrudo, Cotoname, and the Karankawa recorded by Dr. Gatschet are as given by the last named investigator' (p. 10) - no rule stated for any language, Aranama not mentioned there.

sources.citation: Gatschet, Albert S. 1886. Die Karánkawa-Indianer. Globus 49: 123-125. Braunschweig.
sources.note: Earliest printing of the two forms: 'Mein Tónkawe-Informant kannte zwei Wörter ihrer Sprache: himiyána, Wasser; himiána tsáyi! reiche mir Wasser!' (p. 124, right column). Acute accents on the penult of himiyána/himiána and on tsáyi; no statement about accent or stress.
